topic: Finterm.ai: Bloomberg Terminal for Claude Code

key_points: CLI-based financial data tool for coding agents (Claude Code, ChatGPT, etc.)
Founded by Kam and Josh under DXDT Labs Incorporated
Launched as Show HN on Hacker News July 13, 2026
npm install -g @finterm-ai/cli to install
Pricing: $150/month preview ($200/month standard), 3-day free trial
Data delayed up to 15 minutes to keep costs reasonable
Designed to be token-efficient vs MCP or raw API calls
Key features: ticker data bundles, SEC filing diffs, ownership flows, options intelligence, sentiment scoring, Ticker Deep Research
Show HN post by founder Kam on July 13, 2026
Founder's personal story: short thesis on Popmart Labubu, made 16% using LLM-assisted research
Pain point: manual SEC data fetching, copy-pasting into GPT, juggling chat windows
CLI approach chosen because agents perform better with CLI than MCP (fewer tokens)
Batch multiple data calls into one bundle to save tokens
Ticker Deep Research: fetches 600-800 links per ticker, strips 30-40% noise
SEC filing diff: 90-95% of filings are boilerplate, diff shows only important changes
Agent-readable setup guide with install commands, examples, and guardrails
Install: npm install -g @finterm-ai/cli, then finterm setup, finterm prime
Auth: finterm auth login (browser) or FINTERM_API_KEY env var
Without Pro: HTTP 402 SUBSCRIPTION_REQUIRED with upgrade_url
Example workflow: compare 10-Qs for GOOGL, AMZN, MSFT using sec_filing_diff

Full API reference with 12 tools: stock_prices_current, technical_indicators, sec_filings_search, sec_filing_fetch, sec_filing_diff, options_sentiment, options_overview, financial_statements, insider_trades, institutional_holdings, ticker_sentiment, ticker_data
Every response has two-key envelope: finterm (meta) + data or error
OpenAPI spec at https://api.finterm.ai/api/v1/openapi.json
Catalog at https://api.finterm.ai/api/v1/catalog
Published July 14, 2026 — official product introduction
Three tiers: point tools (narrow questions), bundles (combined results), research packages (larger evidence in local data rooms)
Designed for inspectable research: results retain links, timestamps, and caveats
Workflow: finterm prime → choose tool/bundle/package → inspect sources → carry into analysis

stats.fact: Finterm Pro costs $150/month during preview period, $200/month standard
Ticker Deep Research fetches 600-800 links per ticker, strips 30-40% noise
SEC filings are 90-95% boilerplate; Finterm's diff tool shows only the changes
Stock and options data is delayed by up to 15 minutes
Purchased separately, comparable APIs cost $300-450/month vs Finterm Pro at $200/month

Finterm offers 12 distinct tools via CLI: prices, technicals, SEC search/fetch/diff, options sentiment/overview, financial statements, insider trades, institutional holdings, ticker sentiment, ticker data bundle
Launched on Hacker News as Show HN on July 13, 2026 by founder Kam
Company: DXDT Labs Incorporated, founded by Kam and Josh

angles: Finterm positions itself as 'Bloomberg Terminal for Claude Code' — a CLI-first financial data layer for AI agents, not humans
Token efficiency is the core differentiator: CLI beats MCP and raw API calls for agent context windows
The SEC filing diff tool solves a real pain point: 90-95% boilerplate in filings, agents only need the changes
Ticker Deep Research solves the 'SEO spam and noise' problem in web-based financial research
Founder-led product with real trading experience (Popmart short thesis story) adds authenticity
Niche but growing market: developers who trade stocks using Claude Code and other coding agents
Pricing ($150-200/mo) is competitive vs $300-450/mo for comparable APIs purchased separately
Data delay (15 min) is a limitation for active traders but acceptable for research-first use case
